text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Results of last Saturday's local council elections suggest that many political heavyweights have lost their power bases and that new leaders are beginning to emerge on the scene.
- Former presidential candidate Bashir Tofa refutes newspaper reports that he has been arrested.
- More private airlines flying the domestic routes hike fares following approval of 100 percent increase in local air fares by the military government.
- Fuel scarcity in Lagos and neighbouring states worsens, prospects of quick end bleak.
- No change in deadline to liquidate distressed banks by March 31 if they fail to recapitalise, says finance minister Anthony Ani

- Petroleum Trust Fund, which disburses money accruing to the state from a 1994 increase in pump prices, spends 1.25 billion naira to upgrade facilities at a complex in the north where African trade and tourism fair is to be held next week.
- Court sets April 2 for hearing in bail application by 12 dissidents charged with treason over bomb blasts in Nigeria.
- Ladi Olorunyomi, wife of former editor of opposition magazine The News, who left Nigeria in 1994, has been arrested, says her sister in a press statement.
- Demand for foreign exchange at weekly auction rises to $78 million from $66 million last week, says central bank.
- The federal government may have disbursed 250 million naira to each of the five political parties before last Saturday's municipal councils election, sources say.

- News editors of Thisday and TNT newspapers, who were arrested this week over false reports that Lagos state police chief had been reassigned, freed following plea by Lagos state chapter of the Nigerian Union Journalists.
